label_policy.accept: A supported input reproducibly exposes an actionable defect; value is rated separately.
label_policy.downgrade: A reproduced robustness or documentation concern does not warrant treatment as a user-visible compiler bug.
label_policy.reject: The hypothesis is intended, unsupported, producer-impossible, falsified, duplicate, or otherwise non-actionable.
label_policy.defer: The behavior is reproduced but decisive contract or oracle evidence remains unresolved.

findings.title: Postfix property update evaluates its receiver twice
findings.supervision: Reward this discovery pattern. Ordinary valid source must evaluate the postfix property receiver once, but the baseline reads the first object and writes the second after calling the receiver twice.

findings.title: TypedArray.copyWithin traps on an empty source range
findings.supervision: The empty range should be a no-op, so this is a real standard-library defect. Keep its value low because the reversed range resembles conspicuously erroneous user input and is a less useful search target than an ordinary-program miscompile.

findings.title: Typed-array bounds checks are bypassed by signed overflow
findings.supervision: The overflowing public API argument bypasses the promised bounds check and creates an invalid view. Accept the defect but rate it low value because it requires an impossible-sized view request at an extreme integer boundary.

findings.title: Plain property assignment reverses receiver and RHS evaluation
findings.supervision: Direct execution produced receiver-before-RHS order. Omit hypotheses that fail their runtime oracle instead of presenting them as Candidate Findings.

findings.title: Uint16Array.reverse uses a mis-scaled front address
findings.supervision: The current implementation already scales the address correctly and direct execution returns the expected reversed values. Omit the falsified hypothesis.
